docs.title: Welcome to idmtools_calibra
docs.text:
idmtools_calibra is a collection of Python scripts and utilities to aid in model calibration. The idmtools package should be used for streamlining the process of running disease modeling simulations. Additional information can be found at the IDM docs.

See the idmtools documentation for a diagram showing how idmtools and each of the related packages are used in an end-to-end workflow using EMOD as the disease transmission model.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: Follow the steps below to install idmtools_calibra.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
First, ensure the following prerequisites are met.

  • Windows 10 Pro or Enterprise, Linux, or Mac
  • Python >= 3.10 (https://www.python.org/downloads/release)

  • A file that indicates the pip index-url:

    WindowsLinux / Mac

    In C:\Users\Username\pip\pip.ini add the following: INI

    [global]
index-url = https://packages.idmod.org/api/pypi/pypi-production/simple

    In $HOME/.config/pip/pip.conf add the following: INI

    [global]
index-url = https://packages.idmod.org/api/pypi/pypi-production/simple

docs.title: Installation instructions
docs.text:
1. Open a command prompt and create a virtual environment in any directory you choose. The command below names the environment v-calibra, but you may use any desired name:

    Bash
    python -m venv v-calibra

  2. Activate the virtual environment:

    WindowsLinux / Mac Batchfile
    v-calibra\Scripts\activate
    Bash
    source v-calibra/bin/activate

  3. Install idmtools_calibra:

    Bash
    pip install idmtools_calibra

    Note

    If you are on Linux, also run: Bash

    pip install keyrings.alt

  4. When you are finished, deactivate the virtual environment:

    Bash
    deactivate

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: idmtools_calibra is an iterative calibration framework for scientific and epidemic models. It runs parameter sweeps, compares model output to reference data, and updates the sampling strategy until convergence.

docs.title: Calibration workflow
docs.text:
The calibration loop is orchestrated by CalibManager and follows these steps each iteration:

  1. Sample — NextPointAlgorithm.get_samples_for_iteration() generates a set of parameter combinations to evaluate.
  2. Configure — map_sample_to_model_input_fn maps each sample row to the simulation task.
  3. Execute — Simulations are submitted and run via the idmtools Platform (local or COMPS HPC).
  4. Analyze — BaseCalibrationAnalyzer compares model output to reference data and returns a likelihood or error score.
  5. Update — NextPointAlgorithm.set_results_for_iteration() updates the algorithm state with the scores.
  6. Plot — BasePlotter.visualize() generates diagnostic plots for the iteration.

Each iteration's state is written to Calibration.json, enabling resume from any iteration or phase.

docs.title: Key abstractions
docs.text: Class Module Role CalibManager calib_manager Top-level orchestrator NextPointAlgorithm algorithms/next_point_algorithm Abstract base for sampling strategies OptimTool algorithms/optim_tool Adaptive regression-based algorithm (default) IMIS algorithms/imis Incremental Mixture Importance Sampling CalibSite / RMSESite calib_site, rmse_site Wraps reference data and analyzers BaseCalibrationAnalyzer analyzers/base_calibration_analyzer Compares output to reference data IterationState iteration_state Serializable per-iteration state BasePlotter plotters/base_plotter Generates diagnostic plots BaseResampler resamplers/base_resampler Post-calibration resampling strategies

docs.title: Resume support
docs.text:
CalibManager.run_calibration() supports resuming from any iteration and phase:

Python
calib_manager.run_calibration(
    resume=True,
    iteration=2,          # resume from iteration 2
    iter_step='analyze',  # phase: 'commission', 'analyze', 'plot', or 'next_point'
    loop=True,            # continue to next iteration after resuming
    max_iterations=10,    # override max_iterations defined in CalibManager
    backup=True,          # backup Calibration.json before resuming
    dry_run=False,        # set True to preview without executing
)

docs.title: iter_step options
docs.text: Value Behaviour commission Start a new iteration with fresh parameter samples analyze Analyze existing simulation output from the given iteration plot Generate plots for the given iteration only next_point Skip directly to generating the next iteration's samples

docs.title: Example usage
docs.text:
The simplest end-to-end example fits a linear model y = mx + c to solar panel data:

Python
from idmtools_calibra.calib_manager import CalibManager
from idmtools_calibra.algorithms.optim_tool import OptimTool
from idmtools_calibra.resamplers.rmse_site import RMSESite

params = [
    {"Name": "gradient",  "Guess": 0.5, "Min": 0.0, "Max": 2.0, "Dynamic": True},
    {"Name": "intercept", "Guess": 0.0, "Min": -5.0, "Max": 5.0, "Dynamic": True},
]

calib_manager = CalibManager(
    name="solar-calibration",
    task=my_task,
    map_sample_to_model_input_fn=my_map_fn,
    sites=[RMSESite(...)],
    next_point=OptimTool(params, constrain_sample_fn=lambda s: s),
    max_iterations=10,
    num_to_plot=5,
)

calib_manager.run_calibration()

See examples/solar/ for the complete working example, and examples/sir/ for an epidemiological SIR model with multiple output configuration options.
